mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 1.0% compresses equity discount rates and stimulates risk-taking, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days without requiring additional conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 3.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and reduces risk appetite, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS > 150,000.0) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%) indicates robust labor market conditions that boost corporate earnings and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS > 150000.0 and UNRATE < 3.5% fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 4.0%) correlate with economic weakness and reduced corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing starts (HOUST > 1700.0) indicate sustained consumer demand and economic expansion, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1700.0.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts falling below 1700.0 signal weakening consumer demand and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when HOUST < 1700.0.

mechanism_narrative: Weak industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0) combined with high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 290.0) indicates stagflationary pressures that depress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of INDPRO < 100.0 and CPIAUCSL > 290.0 fails to produce negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial expansion regimes (INDPRO > 105.0) signal robust manufacturing output and economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO > 105.0.
